title: sc-theft-offences-definitive-guideline-content_final-web_.pdf — section 24
text:
STEP SIX
Confiscation, compensation and ancillary orders
The court must proceed with a view to making a confiscation order if it is asked to do so by the
prosecutor or if the court believes it is appropriate for it to do so.
Where the offence has resulted in loss or damage the court must consider whether to make a
compensation order.
If the court makes both a confiscation order and an order for compensation and the court believes
the offender will not have sufficient means to satisfy both orders in full, the court must direct that the
compensation be paid out of sums recovered under the confiscation order (section 13 of the Proceeds of
Crime Act 2002).
The court may also consider whether to make ancillary orders. These may include a deprivation order, or
a restitution order.

STEP SEVEN
Reasons
Section 174 of the Criminal Justice Act 2003 imposes a duty to give reasons for, and explain the effect of,
the sentence.
